hook: SCP-500 is a jar of red pills that cure any disease, and there are only a few dozen of them. The article is short and reads like a supply ledger. Keep an eye on the pill count as you go.
whyItMatters: It answers, in miniature, the obvious question of why the Foundation does not simply cure everything: the cure exists, but it cannot be made and it runs out. Its scarcity is the whole design, since a miracle you can count is a miracle people will argue over. The log also works as a web of cross-references, with nearly every entry naming another anomaly the pills were spent on.
thingsToNotice:
The format does the storytelling. Requests and addenda read like an inventory, and the tally drops from fifty-seven to the forty-seven quoted in the description as pills go to cure SCP-008 infection, to tests with other objects, and to one D-class who stole a pill for his hangover and was terminated for it.

The attempts to stretch the supply are the most telling entries. SCP-038 can copy the pills, but the copies cure only about a third of the time and weaken with age, and putting one through SCP-914 on Fine produced a separate object, SCP-427. In the final addendum someone asks to check whether the pills cause an obsessive fixation, and the request is waved off as trivial.

related.note: Addendum 500-9 runs one pill through it on the Fine setting.
The log records it as the object that came out of that 914 run.
Addendum 500-4 uses it to copy the pills, with weak results.
